title: Dynamics and recognition of homeodomain containing protein-DNA complex of IRX4.
authors: Malik, Adil; Jayarathna, Dulari K; Fisher, Mark; Barbhuiya, Tabassum Khair; Gandhi, Neha S; Batra, Jyotsna
one_liner_zh: 该文通过同源建模和分子动力学模拟研究IRX4同源异型域TF与DNA的识别机制及体细胞突变对结合的影响，核心聚焦TF-DNA互作建模，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: Iroquois Homeobox 4 (IRX4) belongs to a family of homeobox TFs having roles in embryogenesis, cell specification, and organ development. Recently, large scale genome-wide association studies and epigenetic studies have highlighted the role of IRX4 and its associated variants in prostate cancer. No studies have investigated and characterized the structural aspect of the IRX4 homeodomain and its potential to bind to DNA. The current study uses sequence analysis, homology modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations to explore IRX4 homeodomain-DNA recognition mechanisms and the role of somatic mutations affecting these interactions. Using publicly available databases, gene expression of IRX4 was found in different tissues, including prostate, heart, skin, vagina, and the protein expression was found in cancer cell lines (HCT166, HEK293), B cells, ascitic fluid, and brain. Sequence conservation of the homeodomain shed light on the importance of N- and C-terminal residues involved in DNA binding. The specificity of IRX4 homodimer bound to consensus human DNA sequence was confirmed by molecular dynamics simulations, representing the role of conserved amino acids including R145, A194, N195, S190, R198, and R199 in binding to DNA. Additional N-terminal residues like T144 and G143 were also found to have specific interactions highlighting the importance of N-terminus of the homeodomain in DNA recognition. Additionally, the effects of somatic mutations, including the conserved Arginine (R145, R198, and R199) residues on DNA binding elucidated the importance of these residues in stabilizing the protein-DNA complex. Secondary structure and hydrogen bonding analysis showed the roles of specific residues (R145, T191, A194, N195, R198, and R199) in maintaining the homogeneity of the structure and its interaction with DNA. The differences in relative binding free energies of all the mutants shed light on the structural modularity of this protein and the dynamics behind protein-DNA interaction. We also have predicted that the C-terminal sequence of the IRX4 homeodomain could act as a potential cell-penetrating peptide, emphasizing the role these small peptides could play in targeting homeobox TFs.
abstract_zh: Iroquois Homeobox 4 (IRX4) 属于一个在胚胎发生、细胞特化和器官发育中具有作用的同源盒转录因子家族。近期，大规模全基因组关联研究和表观遗传学研究强调了IRX4及其相关变异在前列腺癌中的作用。尚无研究调查和表征IRX4同源结构域的结构方面及其与DNA结合的潜力。本研究采用序列分析、同源建模和分子动力学模拟，探讨IRX4同源结构域-DNA识别机制以及影响这些相互作用的体细胞突变的作用。利用公开数据库，发现IRX4的基因表达存在于不同组织中，包括前列腺、心脏、皮肤、阴道，而蛋白表达存在于癌细胞系（HCT166、HEK293）、B细胞、腹水液和脑中。同源结构域的序列保守性揭示了参与DNA结合的N端和C端残基的重要性。通过分子动力学模拟确认了IRX4同源二聚体与共识人类DNA序列结合的特异性，代表了保守氨基酸（包括R145、A194、N195、S190、R198和R199）在DNA结合中的作用。还发现额外的N端残基如T144和G143具有特定相互作用，突显了同源结构域N端在DNA识别中的重要性。此外，体细胞突变（包括保守精氨酸R145、R198和R199残基）对DNA结合的影响阐明了这些残基在稳定蛋白质-DNA复合物中的重要性。二级结构和氢键分析显示了特定残基（R145、T191、A194、N195、R198和R199）在维持结构同质性及其与DNA相互作用中的作用。所有突变体相对结合自由能的差异揭示了该蛋白质的结构模块性以及蛋白质-DNA相互作用背后的动力学。我们还预测IRX4同源结构域的C端序列可能作为潜在的细胞穿透肽，强调了这些小肽在靶向同源盒转录因子中可能发挥的作用。
